findings.issue: D5's DRAFT refusal FAILS OPEN on natural phrasing. `specIsDraft` returns `/\bDRAFT\b/i.test(m[1]) && !/\bRATIFIED\b/i.test(m[1])` — so any Status line that says DRAFT *and* mentions "ratified" is treated as NOT a draft and is BUILT. Executed against the emitted region: `**Status:** DRAFT — not yet ratified` => specDraft false; `**Status:** DRAFT (not yet RATIFIED)` => false; `Status: DRAFT / pending RATIFIED stamp` => false. Only bare `Status: DRAFT` and `Status: DRAFT — awaiting owner ratification` return true. The spec's D5 is unqualified — "/dev-loop **refuses to build any spec still marked DRAFT**" — and /dev-plan is now instructed to write every spec as `Status: DRAFT`, so the very first LLM that writes "Status: DRAFT — not yet ratified" re-opens the draft-laundering path this decision exists to close. The predicate escalates (permits the build) on ambiguity, which is the opposite of the file's own stated `resolve`-typo discipline ("unrecognized NEVER escalates"). The three selftest cases at selftest.mjs:4551-4557 only exercise the unambiguous shapes, so the hole is unpinned.
findings.fix: Drop the `!RATIFIED` escape hatch and make DRAFT dominant: `return /\bDRAFT\b/i.test(m[1]);` (park on ambiguity — the safe direction). If "RATIFIED (formerly DRAFT)" must still build, anchor on the leading token instead: `/^\s*[*_]{0,2}DRAFT\b/i.test(m[1])` plus a DRAFT-anywhere fallback that parks. Add selftest cases for `Status: DRAFT — not yet ratified` and `Status: DRAFT (not yet RATIFIED)` asserting `specDraft === true`.

Executed against the emitted region with the canonical happy-path call `mkMode({}, {mode:'overnight', feature:'add a docket view mode=overnight'}, ratifiedSpec, 'add a docket view mode=overnight')` returns `autonomyMode: 'overnight'` AND a refusal of `overnight` in the same object. That falsehood is logged (`Autonomy REFUSED: …`), carried into the durable attestation record (`modeRefusals`), and — per render.mjs:322-324 — presented to the owner on a park as "a `mode=` claim found in file text and refused". `args.feature` under a typed invocation is not file text; the spec's D1 refusal targets values a repo or PR can *launder*. Writing a demonstrably false statement into the evidence spine on 100% of the feature's happy path corrupts exactly the record R3's coverage mitigation and the Shape-A upgrade evidence depend on.
findings.fix: Exempt the owner-typed channel: skip the `args.feature` scan for the value the owner actually typed, e.g. build the refusal list as `autonomyRefusals([{source:'the spec text', text: spec}, ...(autonomyMode === 'overnight' ? Add a selftest case asserting a legitimate `{mode:'overnight'}` run with `mode=overnight` inside `feature` records ZERO refusals.

'PARKED' : null`, and have render.mjs:321-327 say that a park after a successful land still presents the brief plus the missing-record warning.

findings.fix: Either say it plainly in the docs (amend render.mjs:268 to "…never the owner's main checkout, except a pre-build PARK record, which has no worktree to write to") or route pre-build parks to the gitignored `.claude/veriloop/history/dry-runs/`-style location so the owner's tracked tree stays clean. The only place the override rate is directed is the /dev-plan copy: "Record the owner's **override rate** for this docket … **in the spec**." `grep -rn 'override rate|overrideRate'` across scripts/, .claude/commands/, .claude/workflows/ finds no attestation field, no workflow plumbing, and no selftest beyond a copy-presence check. The attestation gained `autonomyMode`, `parked`, `modeRefusals` and nothing that carries the docket outcome. Since the spec names the measured override rate as "the evidence — and the only evidence — a later Shape-A upgrade could stand on", leaving it only in prose inside a spec file makes it unmeasurable by the machinery that would consume it.
findings.fix: Either add a nullable `docket: { entries, overrides, overrideRate }` field to `attestationFrom` and have /dev-loop accept it via `args` when the docket answer launches the build, or take it back to the owner as an explicit acceptance-4 deviation. findings.issue: `answeredEntries` is a permanently-empty field. `parkedState` hard-codes `[]`, nothing ever appends to it, and no code path reads it — yet its comment claims "a resumed run reads it to know which docket entries were already answered, and an answered entry is NEVER re-opened (D6)". The guarantee is asserted by an empty array, not implemented.
findings.fix: Either drop the field until a resume path exists, or downgrade the comment and the assertion message to what is true ("a placeholder for a future resume path; nothing populates it today"). Do not let a test message credit an unimplemented guarantee.

findings.issue: D5's DRAFT refusal — "the tap's teeth" — FAILS OPEN on the only real DRAFT spec in this repo. The predicate is `/\bDRAFT\b/i.test(m[1]) && !/\bRATIFIED\b/i.test(m[1])`, so any Status line that contains the substring RATIFIED disables the guard — including the negation "NOT RATIFIED". I sliced the `veriloop:autonomy` region out of the emitted workflow and ran it against all 18 specs in `.claude/veriloop/specs/`: `constitution-enforcer-partition.md:7` reads `**Status:** DRAFT — NOT RATIFIED. Two premise challenges below are UNRESOLVED.` and the predicate returns FALSE → /dev-loop adopts it as BINDING and builds it. That is exactly the draft-laundering path D5 was written to kill, live on a file sitting in the corpus today. Two more shapes confirmed BUILDS by the same probe: a blockquoted decoy earlier in the file (`> Status: RATIFIED (example)` … `**Status:** DRAFT`), because the leading class `[\s>*_-]*` accepts `>` and `.match()` takes the FIRST hit anywhere in the document; and `**Status:** DRAFT (to be ratified 2026)`. The ambiguity resolves toward BUILD, the opposite of the safe direction this same file mandates for the `resolve` typo rule and for unrecognized `mode` values.
findings.fix: Invert to a positive ratification test so ambiguity parks: take the first Status line and treat the spec as buildable ONLY when it affirmatively ratifies — e.g. `return !/^\s*(?:\*|_)*RATIFIED\b/i.test(m[1])` — and drop `>` from the leading class so a quoted example cannot pre-empt the real line. Add red/green selftest cases for `DRAFT — NOT RATIFIED`, the blockquote decoy, and `DRAFT (to be ratified …)` beside the existing D5 case at scripts/selftest.mjs:4526-4532.

findings.issue: The launch grant is neither tap-gated nor scoped. That prose sits in the same context /dev-plan deliberately fills with untrusted repo text — it holds Read/Grep/Glob over the whole tree including `fixtures/hostile-ci/`, plus `Bash(git log:*)`/`git show:*` output (PR/commit bodies). This command's entire stated security property is that owner ratification severs `repo text → generated personas → council → spec → background implementer prompts`; an unscoped SlashCommand grant adds a shorter edge to that same path whose only gate is model compliance with an instruction the injected text is competing against. It also puts a capability delta on every mode-absent run, which acceptance 1 says must behave as before. (Fairly: /dev-plan already holds `Task`, so this is a widening rather than a first breach — but it is the direct, sanctioned route to launching a build that pushes a branch, and the spec explicitly asked for it to be inert.)

Then tighten the selftest at scripts/selftest.mjs:4577: it currently matches only `/^allowed-tools:.*\bSlashCommand\b/m`, which a bare unscoped grant satisfies — assert the scoped form instead.

I ran the sliced region with this feature's real invocation shape (`{mode:'overnight'}`, the ratified spec body, `feature: 'build the headless-autonomy feature mode=overnight'`): result is `autonomyMode = overnight` together with FIVE recorded refusals — four from the spec body of `headless-autonomy.md` itself, one from `args.feature`. lenses.summary: NO-GO. The gate is green (lint exit 0; selftest 593 ok / 0 failed) and the mechanical work is genuinely strong — the autonomy region is sliced-and-executed rather than asserted in a comment, the cap carve-out is pinned on both branches, the sever sentence is byte-identical with R1 recorded adjacent, no timeout construct exists on any of the three surfaces, and the template↔workflow and manifest↔workflow parity checks are clean. But three spec-level defects survive the green gate. (1) `specIsDraft` returns FALSE for `Status: DRAFT — NOT RATIFIED` because the substring `RATIFIED` matches — I ran the shipped predicate against every spec in the repo and the ONE real draft, `constitution-enforcer-partition.md`, sails through; D5's entire stated purpose ("kills draft-laundering") fails on the only file in the repo it was written for, and the selftest's two DRAFT phrasings never touch it. (2) `/dev-plan` now writes every spec `Status: DRAFT` "always, in every mode", but the only instruction that flips it to RATIFIED is Step 3.4, explicitly scoped `(mode=overnight only)` — so an ordinary interactive run leaves DRAFT on disk and the new unconditional refusal parks it, breaking acceptance 1 for the mode-absent path. (3) Acceptance 4's final clause — "either shape's override/decision record lands in the attestation" — is silently dropped: the override rate is recorded in the spec prose only, `/dev-loop` receives no docket, and `attestationFrom` has no field for it, which leaves the measured override rate (the sole ratified evidence basis for a future Shape-A upgrade, per the Status block and R4) as unqueryable prose. Beyond those: every legitimate owner-typed `mode=overnight` run self-reports a bogus laundering refusal because `args.feature` IS `$ARGUMENTS` (executed and confirmed), the "no brief on PARKED" doc claim is false for both run-time park paths, the pre-build park writes into the owner's main checkout, and the `generate.mjs` "no manifest key" comment is false (proven: `interview_answers.autonomy` is emitted).

findings.issue: `specIsDraft` uses `!/\bRATIFIED\b/i.test(m[1])` as its escape hatch, so any status line that says the words "NOT RATIFIED" is classified as NOT a draft. I ran the shipped predicate (marker-sliced out of the emitted workflow) over all 18 specs in `.claude/veriloop/specs/`: the ONE real draft in this repo — `constitution-enforcer-partition.md:7`, `**Status:** DRAFT — NOT RATIFIED. Two premise challenges below are UNRESOLVED.` — returns `specDraft = false`. Trace: matched status text `"** DRAFT — NOT RATIFIED. …"`, hasDRAFT true, hasRATIFIED true ⇒ predicate false. `/dev-loop` would adopt that un-ratified spec as BINDING and build it. This is exactly the draft-laundering path D5 exists to kill, defeated by the most natural phrasing of a draft status, and the gate stays green because the selftest's two cases only cover `**Status:** DRAFT` and `Status: DRAFT — awaiting the docket` (scripts/selftest.mjs:4527-4534) — neither is the phrasing already sitting in the repo.
findings.fix: Require an AFFIRMATIVE ratification stamp instead of a bare substring: `const s = m[1]; const ratified = /\bRATIFIED\b/i.test(s) && !/\b(not|un-?)\s*ratified\b/i.test(s); return /\bDRAFT\b/i.test(s) && !ratified;`. Add `**Status:** DRAFT — NOT RATIFIED.` (lifted from the real in-repo spec) to the both-directions selftest case so the phrasing that broke it is the one that pins it.

findings.issue: Step 3.1 mandates writing every spec with `Status: DRAFT` — "always, in every mode". The only IMPERATIVE that flips it is Step 3.4, whose heading is `**The docket answer LAUNCHES the build (\`mode=overnight\` only).**` — "Answering the docket flips the spec to `Status: RATIFIED`". Step 3.3, the interactive ratification, ends at "owner ratification cuts it" plus the residual-risk note and never instructs rewriting the file; Step 4 then says "Once the spec is ratified, offer to run `/dev-loop` with it". So on the mode-absent path the file on disk still says DRAFT, and `/dev-loop`'s new UNCONDITIONAL refusal (template :1108) parks the run the owner just ratified. That contradicts acceptance 1 ("Mode absent ⇒ behavior byte-identical to today (both commands)") and makes /dev-plan → /dev-loop unusable for ordinary features. The author already spotted this class of break and patched the /dev-loop confirm-and-go branch (render.mjs:249, "write the file with `Status: RATIFIED`, never DRAFT, or branch 1's DRAFT refusal will park the run you just confirmed") — the /dev-plan branch did not get the same treatment. No selftest asserts the flip; the D5 assertion (selftest.mjs:4610) only pins the overnight sentence.
findings.fix: Move the flip into Step 3.3 unconditionally: on the owner's ratification, re-write the spec file's `Status:` line to `RATIFIED — BINDING (owner, <date>)` in EVERY mode, and leave Step 3.4 to the launch trigger alone. Pin it with an assertion that the interactive ratification step itself names the DRAFT→RATIFIED rewrite.

findings.issue: Acceptance criterion 4 ends: "either shape's override/decision record lands in the attestation." It does not. `/dev-plan` records the override rate "in the spec" (render.mjs:597) and nothing carries it further: Step 3.4's launch call passes only the ratified spec and `mode`, the workflow has no `args.docket`/override input (grep for `override` across the template and emitted workflow returns only `.overrides.md` persona paths), and `attestationFrom` gained `autonomyMode` / `parked` / `modeRefusals` but no docket or override field. The measured override rate is, per the Status block and R4, the ONLY evidence a Shape-A upgrade may stand on — the resolve-to-clean D8 precedent right above the new fields (`resolveMode`, `rawConcerns`, `confirmedConcerns`, commented "A future auto-merge predicate READS these; it must never re-derive them") is exactly the shape this needed and did not get. The selftest asserts only that the /dev-plan copy contains "Record the owner's **override rate**" (selftest.mjs:4602), i.e. that the prose exists — never that the record reaches the attestation.
findings.fix: Carry the docket forward from /dev-plan's launch call as `args.docket = { entries: [...], overridden: <n>, total: <n> }`, and add a nullable `docket: evidence.docket || null` beside `autonomyMode` in `attestationFrom` (it rides the same recursive redactor). Add a selftest case building a synthetic overnight evidence object and asserting the override record survives into `history/<ts>.json`, plus the mode-absent null.

findings.issue: `autonomyRefusals` scans `args.feature` as untrusted "file text", but `/dev-loop` Step 2 passes `args = { feature: "$ARGUMENTS" }` (render.mjs:265) — `args.feature` IS the owner-typed invocation, the one channel D1 designates as the ONLY trusted source. I executed the sliced region with a realistic invocation (`a = { mode:'overnight', feature:'mode=overnight add a retry to the fetcher' }`) and got `autonomyMode: 'overnight'` alongside a refusal: `source: 'args.feature', claimed: 'overnight', reason: 'a \`mode=overnight\` value found in args.feature is REFUSED — file text can never raise autonomy'`. So EVERY legitimate overnight run logs a laundering alarm about the owner's own typed words, writes it into `modeRefusals` in the attestation, and — per render.mjs:322-324 — has the main session present it to the owner as "a `mode=` claim found in file text and refused". A control that cries wolf on its own happy path is the alarm-fatigue failure that makes it worthless, and it corrupts the one machine-readable artifact R3 leans on. It also fires 4 times on this repo's own `headless-autonomy.md` spec text, which merely documents the mode.
findings.fix: Drop `{ source: 'args.feature', text: feature }` from the scan list at :128 (the owner typed it; `args.mode` is the only channel that acts on it), or suppress refusals whose `claimed` value equals the owner-typed `a.mode` for this run. Keep the spec-text scan. Update the selftest's args.feature case accordingly and add a case asserting an owner-typed `mode=overnight` invocation records ZERO refusals.

findings.issue: The new copy states: "**If `result.terminalState === \"PARKED\"` there is NO brief** — a park is not a finished run. Present `result.parked` instead… Say plainly… that the record was serialized to `.claude/veriloop/history/`". Both clauses are false for the two RUN-TIME park paths. `terminalState` is `parked ? 'PARKED' : null` (template :1489) and `parked` is set at Land (:1341, PARK-TERMINAL after a full gate) and at Report (:1454, unconfirmed attestation write) — in both cases the return object DOES carry `brief`, `gateHistory`, `blockers`, `concerns`, `branch` and `worktree` (:1467-1506). Only `parkBeforeBuild` returns without a brief. So the doc instructs the main session to discard the compressed gate evidence on exactly the runs where the owner most needs it to triage. Worse, in the attestation-park case the reason for the park IS that the record could not be confirmed written — the doc tells the presenter to assert it was serialized.
findings.fix: Split the branch: pre-build parks (`!result.brief`) present `result.parked` alone; run-time parks present the brief AND the park banner. Drop or condition the "the record was serialized" sentence — the attestation-park case must say the record is MISSING and name `result.parked.context` (which already carries the expected path).

findings.issue: `parkBeforeBuild` deliberately omits the `wt(...)` clause and instructs the agent to "Write this run's PARK RECORD into the owner's checkout at $REPO" at `$REPO/.claude/veriloop/history/<ts>.json`. Two problems: (a) it contradicts the loop's own promise two sections earlier in the same command — "It then runs autonomously on a dedicated **git worktree + branch** (never the owner's main checkout)" (render.mjs:270) and the `wt()` helper's "never the owner's main checkout" (template :347); (b) `.claude/veriloop/history/` is a TRACKED directory (only `history/dry-runs/` is in the machine-owned .gitignore block) and is itself a protected-path class (`history`), so a park leaves an untracked file dirtying the owner's main working tree, where a later `git add -A` sweeps it into an unrelated commit. It is also invisible to `lint-bundle`'s committed-record scan until that happens. Note the DRAFT park is UNCONDITIONAL by mode, so this fires on ordinary interactive runs too, not just overnight ones.
findings.fix: Either route pre-build parks to the already-gitignored `history/dry-runs/`-style path (e.g. `history/parks/`, added to the machine-owned .gitignore block in the same change), or return the park record in `result` and let the `/dev-loop` command write it. Whichever is chosen, say it out loud in the Mode/When-it-returns copy — the docs currently promise the opposite.

findings.issue: `SlashCommand` is added to /dev-plan's `allowed-tools` UNCONDITIONALLY, for every adopter and every invocation. Frontmatter has no mode signal, so this capability exists on mode-absent runs too — where the command's own copy claims "With `mode` absent this command behaves exactly as it did before the mode existed" (render.mjs:578) and "With `mode` absent, nothing here fires" (:751). Today /dev-plan cannot invoke any slash command; after this change it can, and the only thing holding it inert is prose at :748-751. /dev-plan ingests untrusted repo text (spec bodies, generated personas, PR/request text — the very laundering path the sever sentence names three lines above), and it now holds that text in a context with a build-launching grant. The spec ratified answer-launches-build, so the grant itself is in-scope; the undisclosed mode-absent expansion is not.
findings.fix: Do not silently widen acceptance 1: state in the Mode section and the CHANGELOG's "What did NOT change" paragraph that the `SlashCommand` grant is present on every /dev-plan run regardless of mode and is held inert by instruction only, and record it as a residual risk beside R1 (it is MUST-ESCALATE class (b), danger-surface authority expansion). If the grant can be narrowed to `SlashCommand(/dev-loop:*)`, do that too.

findings.issue: The JSDoc on `assertAutonomyNotRaisedByFile` asserts: "DELIBERATELY EMITS NOTHING. No `config` field, **no manifest key**, no `VERILOOP.*` entry". The manifest-key half is false. `main()` writes `interview_answers: interview` wholesale (generate.mjs:600), so an accepted `autonomy` value lands in the manifest — proven by running the shipped generator against a scratch repo with `{"autonomy":"interactive"}`: `manifest.interview_answers = {"autonomy":"interactive"}`. The selftest's non-emission assertion (selftest.mjs:4570) checks only the spliced `VERILOOP` config, so the comment overclaims relative to its own evidence, and the CHANGELOG repeats the narrower (correct) workflow-config claim while this comment states the broader false one. The laundering path stays closed — a re-run reads `pm.interview_answers` back as `interview` (generate.mjs:430) and the assert refuses it — but a false comment on the ownership/emission boundary is exactly the drift this beat exists to catch.
findings.fix: Correct the comment to "no `config` field, no `VERILOOP.*` entry, and no workflow↔manifest parity row — the value does persist in `interview_answers`, where a re-run reads it back and this same assert refuses anything but `interactive`", and extend the selftest assertion to pin that round-trip refusal.

findings.issue: The `interview.json` schema block ("Schema (every field optional)") is the repo's key inventory for that file and is not updated with the new `autonomy` key — even though `/dev-loop`, `/dev-plan`, README and SKILL.md's own new prose all tell adopters `interview.autonomy` exists and that any value but `interactive` FAILS THE BUILD. `resolve_default` sits two lines above documenting that exact fail-the-build pattern, so the precedent for the entry is in the same block. An adopter reading the schema has no way to learn the key exists or that it is refusal-guarded (CLAUDE.md rule 6, doc/schema sync).
findings.fix: Add to the schema block: `"autonomy": "interactive",  // default absent; the ONLY value a file may set. Any other value (overnight/headless/typo) FAILS THE BUILD — file text can never raise autonomy; mode=overnight is accepted only from the owner-typed invocation.`

findings.issue: `const parkTerminal = autonomyMode === 'overnight' && (state.effectiveVerdict === 'FAIL' || noProgressHalt);` is the whole of acceptance 3's "FAIL parks terminally with the worktree preserved", and nothing pins it. The selftest covers park SERIALIZATION through `attestationFrom` (:4620-4645) and the mode/DRAFT predicates via marker slices, but the park CONTROL FLOW — this expression, the `noProgressHalt` flag set at :1280, the `if (specDraft) return await parkBeforeBuild(...)` gate at :1108, and the overnight-no-spec gate at :1118 — is unasserted, so a later refactor that drops the mode condition or reorders the Land branches stays green. The resolve-to-clean precedent shows this is fixable: `shouldFix`/`progressed` are marker-sliced and executed for exactly this reason.
findings.fix: Wrap the park decision in a `veriloop:autonomygate` marker pair (or hoist it into a pure `parkTerminalFor(autonomyMode, verdict, noProgressHalt)` helper inside the existing `veriloop:autonomy` region) and add a case table: overnight+FAIL ⇒ true, overnight+no-progress ⇒ true, overnight+PASS ⇒ false, interactive+FAIL ⇒ false.
